sections.title: Embedded Systems and IoT
sections.summary: I build sensing, computing and display hardware that measures, processes and reports, and I have used it in the Smart Helmet and HYDRA.

capabilities.title: Microcontroller and single-board computer platforms
capabilities.description: I program and interface Arduino and ESP32 microcontrollers and Raspberry Pi single-board computers as the sensing, control and processing core of my prototypes. In the Smart Helmet, a Raspberry Pi is the controller of a wearable that I coached my student team to build and on which I am a named inventor. In HYDRA, as project author, I joined sensors, cameras and a water dispenser in one kiosk.
capabilities.review: Which board HYDRA uses, and whether Arduino and ESP32 appear in any project.

capabilities.title: Firmware and hardware interfaces
capabilities.description: I write C/C++ firmware and connect modules over I²C (Inter-Integrated Circuit), SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface) and UART (serial) links. In HYDRA, I connected the I²C-based MAX30102 pulse oximeter so that a finger pulse reading sits alongside the camera-based measurements.
capabilities.review: C/C++ and the three buses come from your request; confirm where each was used.

capabilities.title: Sensor integration
capabilities.description: I read physiological, gas, motion, environmental, distance and camera sensors and pass clean data to analysis software. The Smart Helmet uses an MQ-2 gas sensor, an accelerometer and a GPS module; HYDRA uses a MAX30102 sensor and cameras. I also work with temperature, humidity, light, ultrasonic and infrared distance sensors.
tools: MAX30102 pulse oximetry and heart rate
capabilities.review: Environmental and distance sensors have no project evidence.

capabilities.title: Connected devices and edge processing
capabilities.description: I build prototypes that collect data on the device, run the analysis locally or on a nearby computer, and report through a display, GPS location and a cellular GSM link. The Smart Helmet works this way: it monitors the wearer, analyses the readings and supports an emergency response. HYDRA analyses its measurements and reports the volume of water to dispense.
capabilities.review: TinyML / TensorFlow Lite and any Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or MQTT use: confirm.

sections.title: Robotics, Automation and System Integration
sections.summary: I build microcontroller- and computer-controlled prototypes, I am trained in industrial automation (PLCs, SCADA and industrial robots), and I coach student robotics teams.

capabilities.title: Sensor and actuator integration
capabilities.description: I connect sensors to actuators and coordinate them from one controller. In HYDRA, a single control system runs the cameras, the pulse sensor and the pump that dispenses the volume of water the analysis suggests.
capabilities.review: Motors and servos have no project evidence.

capabilities.title: Control logic and automated operating sequences
capabilities.description: I define the order in which a device senses, decides and acts. HYDRA follows a scan, analyse and dispense cycle, and the Smart Helmet keeps monitoring its wearer and raises an alert when it detects a problem.
capabilities.review: Smart Helmet alert thresholds: confirm how they are set.

capabilities.title: Workflow and process automation
capabilities.description: I connect apps, data sources and devices into automated workflows, using triggers, API calls, data transformations, notifications and scheduled runs. I build them with tools such as n8n, Node-RED, Zapier and Make.
capabilities.review: Which of these tools you use, and an example workflow (for example sensor data into a notification).

capabilities.title: Industrial automation (training)
capabilities.description: I have trained in programmable logic controllers (PLC), supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems and industrial robots. This extends the embedded control I do in my own prototypes to factory-style automation.
capabilities.review: Where and when you trained, which PLC brand and language (for example ladder logic), which SCADA software and robot brand, and any certificate. Industrial experience is not claimed.

capabilities.title: Robotics software and simulation
capabilities.description: Before I build hardware, I simulate mobile robots, manipulators and perception pipelines in virtual environments. I use Gazebo with ROS 2 for mobile robots and navigation, NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab for AI robotics and learning-based control, CoppeliaSim for robot arms and custom robot prototypes, and Webots for teaching and research simulation.

capabilities.title: Prototype integration, troubleshooting and testing
capabilities.description: I combine hardware, firmware and software into a working prototype, then test and debug it as a system. I did this myself as the author of HYDRA, and I guided my student team through the same prototyping and testing on the Smart Helmet.

capabilities.title: Robotics coaching
capabilities.description: I coach student teams in robotics and intelligent-machine competitions, and I have been recognised as a Winning Coach in Robotics and Intelligent Machine under the Department of Education.

sections.title: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Computer Vision
sections.summary: I build models and image-analysis workflows that turn data into measurements, classifications and forecasts, and I have applied them in HYDRA, RETINA, VISION, HYSEIS and SAFARIS.

capabilities.title: Classical machine learning
capabilities.description: I train classifiers and forecasters on engineered features and historical data. In RETINA, I implemented a Random Forest (200 trees, depth 4, balanced class weights) on fractal features. HYDRA uses a Support Vector Machine on its combined measurements, and in HYSEIS I combined XGBoost with the Omori–Utsu and Gutenberg–Richter models to forecast aftershocks.

capabilities.title: Deep learning
capabilities.description: I build and apply convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image classification and U-Net models for segmentation, working in PyTorch and TensorFlow / Keras. VISION classifies medical images of the lungs, brain and skin with a CNN, and HYDRA uses U-Net segmentation on its eye scan.
capabilities.review: Which project used PyTorch and which used TensorFlow/Keras; training details.

capabilities.title: Image segmentation and feature extraction
capabilities.description: I develop image-processing workflows that isolate the relevant region and extract measurable features. In RETINA, I used OpenCV with CLAHE contrast enhancement, black-hat morphology and thresholding to isolate the vessel network and measure fractal and texture features. In my MATLAB skin-lesion tool, a photograph passes through grey conversion, enhancement, binarisation and segmentation before the tool reports Energy and Contrast values.

capabilities.title: Object detection
capabilities.description: I detect and localise objects in images. In HYDRA, I use YOLOv11 to find the urine reagent strip and its specific-gravity (SG) pad in the camera image.
capabilities.review: Detection details come from your message: confirm the training data and results.

capabilities.title: Data annotation and dataset preparation
capabilities.description: I label images with boxes, polygons and masks, then clean, split and version the datasets for training. For HYDRA, I annotated the urine test strips and their SG pads in CVAT, and I also work with Roboflow and Label Studio.
capabilities.review: Roboflow and Label Studio use; dataset sizes.

capabilities.title: Model evaluation and interpretation
capabilities.description: I evaluate models with stratified k-fold cross-validation, confusion matrices, precision, recall and F1, and ROC / Youden's J cutoffs, as I did in RETINA. In VISION, I explain each prediction with a Grad-CAM heatmap, a probability chart and training curves.

capabilities.title: Wider machine-learning topics
capabilities.description: I have working knowledge of natural language processing, predictive modelling and anomaly detection, as I state in my skin-lesion project description.
capabilities.review: Confirm the depth; this is a statement of understanding rather than a project.

capabilities.title: Analog and digital circuit simulation
capabilities.description: I check circuit behaviour before I build it. I use LTspice for analog circuits, Logisim Evolution for digital logic design, and NI Multisim when I want analog and digital circuits in one environment.

capabilities.title: Microcontroller and firmware simulation

I use Proteus VSM for firmware with its surrounding circuitry and Wokwi for Arduino, ESP32 and IoT projects online. I also use Tinkercad Circuits, SimulIDE, PICsimLab and Renode for real-time microcontroller, virtual-peripheral and emulated embedded-system work.

capabilities.title: Enclosure and mechanical design
capabilities.description: I model enclosures and mounts for my prototype hardware in CAD software such as SolidWorks and Fusion 360, and I check their fit before anything is made.
capabilities.review: Which CAD software, and an example part or enclosure.

capabilities.title: Hardware prototyping and testing
capabilities.description: I assemble and test prototype hardware at the bench: the Smart Helmet's sensing and display unit, which my student team built under my coaching, and the HYDRA kiosk, which I authored. This rests on my BS in Electronics Engineering and Computer Science, my MS in Electronics and Telecommunications Engineering and my licence as a Registered Electronics Engineer.

sections.title: Programming, Applications and Data Systems
sections.summary: I write the software that serves my models, stores and processes data, and presents results to engineers.

capabilities.title: Programming
capabilities.description: I write Python for analysis and applications, C/C++ for microcontrollers, MATLAB for image processing, JavaScript for interfaces and SQL for data. RETINA is my clearest example: I wrote its Python, JavaScript and SQL myself, and my skin-lesion tool is built in MATLAB.

capabilities.title: Model-serving applications
capabilities.description: I build web applications that accept an upload, run a model or analysis and return the result. RETINA is a Flask application with 18 routes that I wrote, and I built the browser applications VISION and SAFARIS to work the same way.
capabilities.review: Framework used in VISION and SAFARIS.

capabilities.title: Databases and data handling
capabilities.description: I store analysis history and reference data in SQLite using SQL, process arrays with NumPy, export results to CSV, as in RETINA, and I also work with tables in pandas. I developed the School Information and Data Management System, which manages student records, attendance and grading.
capabilities.review: pandas is not used in the RETINA source; confirm where you have used it.

capabilities.title: Engineering interfaces and reports
capabilities.description: I present results as dashboards, interactive maps, plots and printable reports. RETINA produces plots, PDF reports, a 12-step animated simulation and video export. HYSEIS shows its aftershock forecasts on an interactive Leaflet map, VISION shows probability charts, and the school system gives statistical dashboards of learners.

capabilities.title: Rapid demos and front-end frameworks
capabilities.description: I turn models into quick demos and component-based interfaces with Streamlit, Gradio, React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS.
capabilities.review: Condensed from the earlier 16-card list. No project evidence; keep only the tools you have used.

capabilities.title: Development workflow
capabilities.description: I use version control, notebooks and scripting to keep my work organised and repeatable: Git and GitHub, Jupyter, VS Code, and PowerShell and Bash. In RETINA, I fix the random seeds so that the model results can be reproduced.
capabilities.review: Git/GitHub, Jupyter and VS Code use: no repository history was supplied.

sections.title: Mathematical Modelling, Research and Validation
sections.summary: I turn a scientific question into defined, computable and testable quantities, and I have done this in RETINA and HYSEIS.

capabilities.title: Mathematical modelling and numerical analysis
capabilities.description: In RETINA, I implemented a box-counting fractal dimension (the least-squares slope of ln N(ε) against ln(1/ε)) and a 16-region local analysis of the vessel network. In HYSEIS, I applied the Omori–Utsu aftershock decay and Gutenberg–Richter magnitude–frequency models.

capabilities.title: Statistical analysis and research design
capabilities.description: I frame measurable research questions and test the relationships between measures. In RETINA, I computed Pearson and Spearman correlations with p-values and r², standardised each deviation against a healthy reference with z-scores, and derived ROC / Youden's J cutoffs.

capabilities.title: Experimental testing and evaluation
capabilities.description: I design evaluations and compare my results against references: cross-validated metrics in RETINA, and worked example scenarios and runs in HYSEIS and my MATLAB tool. Each of my projects states whether its evidence is source code, a demonstration or a competition result.

capabilities.title: Technical documentation and communication
capabilities.description: I document designs, methods and results for different readers: project write-ups, a research study draft, a method article on how RETINA measures vessel complexity, and more than ten years of teaching engineering mathematics and mentoring student research.
